# Before you start {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## What you already have

From the Session 01 pre-session, on the machine you are holding:

::: {.tight}
- VS Codium, with its integrated terminal
- A Python environment that imports numpy, pandas and scikit-learn
- Ollama serving Qwen 2.5 Coder, verified with the wifi off
- aider, editing real files from the terminal
:::

::: {.warn}
If any of those is missing, fix it before this. Everything below assumes a
working workstation.
:::

## What this session adds

You are about to start working **in a group of three**, on a shared codebase.

::: {.tight}
- A place to put the work where all three of you can reach it
- A record of who contributed what, which the course uses in assessment
- A way to disagree with each other's code without losing either version
:::

::: {.muted}
Budget 45 minutes. Same conventions as before: **download** means a browser,
**VS Codium terminal** means the panel inside the editor.
:::

## `XX` means *your group number*

Wherever a command on these slides shows **`XX`**, type your own two-digit group number instead.

| If you are | you type |
|---|---|
| Group 1 | `group-01` |
| Group 7 | `group-07` |
| Group 10 | `group-10` |

::: {.warn}
Never type the letters `XX`. Every example from here on uses **group 07** — substitute your own.
:::

::: {.muted}
You get your group number in Session 01. Do not guess it.
:::

## Why the record matters here

Group marks reward the group. This course checks that the group mark reflects
what each member did, using four records — and one of them is your commit
history.

::: {.check}
See [`GROUP-ASSESSMENT.md`](../../GROUP-ASSESSMENT.md) for the full policy. The
short version: work that cannot be attributed to you counts as work you did not
do.
:::

# Git {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Install Git

::: {.get}
download
:::

Go to **git-scm.com/downloads** and run the installer for your system. Accept
every default.

::: {.muted}
macOS may already have it. The next slide tells you how to check.
:::

## Tell git who you are

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
git --version
git config --global user.name  "Your Full Name"
git config --global user.email "your.name@hec.ca"
```

::: {.warn}
**Use your real name and your university email.** Commits from
`unknown@localhost` cannot be attributed to you, and unattributed work counts
as work you did not do.
:::

## Report it to me

Bring your exact `user.name` and `user.email` to Session 02.

::: {.check}
```bash
git config --global user.name
git config --global user.email
```
:::

::: {.muted}
If your git email differs from the one on the roster, your commits will not be
matched to you, and the contribution report will show you as having done
nothing. This takes ten seconds to prevent and is tedious to repair.
:::

## What a commit is

A commit is a **labelled snapshot** of your work, with an author and a message.

::: {.tight}
- It is not a backup — it is a statement about what changed and why
- The message is written for the person reading it in six weeks
- That person is usually you
:::

::: {.warn}
`git commit -m "update"` tells nobody anything. `"Fix leakage: move scaler
inside the CV pipeline"` tells them everything.
:::

# GitHub {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Create your account

1. Go to **github.com** and choose **Sign up**.
2. Use an email you will still have after you graduate.
3. Pick a username you would put on a CV — this is a professional record.
4. Verify the email GitHub sends you.
5. Enable **two-factor authentication** when prompted. GitHub requires it.

::: {.shot}
[ github.com/signup — email, password, username, then a verification step ]
:::

::: {.muted}
Free accounts include unlimited private repositories.
:::

## You do not create a repository

There is **one repository for the whole course** — the one you downloaded as a ZIP in Session 01.

::: {.tight}
- `main` is the instructor's branch. You never push to it.
- Your group gets **one branch**, `group-NN` — your own number.
- Everything your group produces is committed there.
:::

::: {.check}
**Send your GitHub username to me.** I add you as a collaborator by hand. You cannot push until I
have.
:::

## Where your work goes

```
github.com/warint/quantitative-methods
│
├── main         ← mine
├── group-01
├── group-02
└── group-07     ← yours (your own number)
```

Deliverables live in the session folder:

```
NN-session-name/02-lab/submissions/group-07/
```

## Why one repository

::: {.warn}
Your commit history is one of four records used to check that all three of you did the work, and
`scripts/assess.py contributions` reads it **from this repository**.
:::

::: {.muted}
Work pushed anywhere else is invisible to it — and invisible work counts as work you did not do.
:::

# Connecting it {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Clone the course repository

This **replaces** the Session 01 ZIP. Delete the unzipped folder after, so you
cannot edit the wrong copy.

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
git clone https://github.com/warint/quantitative-methods.git qmib
cd qmib
```

Then `File → Open Folder…` and choose `qmib`.

::: {.check}
Rebuild the environment inside the clone — `python3 -m venv .venv`, activate,
`pip install -r requirements.txt`.
:::

## Your password will not work

When you first push, GitHub asks for credentials and **rejects your account
password**. It wants a *token*.

1. github.com → your avatar → **Settings**
2. **Developer settings** → **Personal access tokens** → **Tokens (classic)**
3. **Generate new token**, tick the **`repo`** scope, set an expiry

## Using the token

4. Copy the token — **it is shown once**
5. Paste it when git asks for your *password*

::: {.check}
```bash
git config --global credential.helper store
```

Stores it, so you are asked only once.
:::

## The round trip

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal · on your group branch
:::

```bash
# group 07 shown — use your own number
mkdir -p 02-geometry-of-least-squares/02-lab/submissions/group-07
echo "# Group 07" > \
  02-geometry-of-least-squares/02-lab/submissions/group-07/NOTES.md

git add 02-geometry-of-least-squares/02-lab/submissions/group-07/
git commit -m "Add group 07 notes"
git push
```

## What just happened

Refresh the repository page, switch to your group's branch, and the file is there.

::: {.check}
Edit locally → commit → push → visible to your group. Everything this term is a
variation on that loop.
:::

::: {.warn}
Write **only inside your own `submissions/group-NN/` folder.** Never edit the
course files or the top-level `README.md` — those are mine, and `main` is
protected.
:::

## Getting other people's work

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
git pull
```

::: {.warn}
**Pull before you start working, every time.** Most merge conflicts are caused
by someone editing a stale copy of a file for two hours.
:::

# Working together {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## Branches

Work on a branch, not directly on `main`:

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
git checkout group-07      # your group's branch
git pull                   # take teammates' work first
# ... work, commit ...
git push
```

::: {.check}
Then open a **pull request** on GitHub so a teammate reads the change before it
joins `main`. That review *is* the group work.
:::

## When two of you edit the same lines

Git stops and marks the conflict in the file:

```
<<<<<<< HEAD
alpha = 0.05
=======
alpha = 0.01
>>>>>>> their-branch
```

::: {.tight}
- Delete the markers and keep the version you both agree on
- `git add` the file, then `git commit`
:::

::: {.muted}
A conflict is not a failure. It is git refusing to guess which of you was right.
:::

## What aider does to your history

aider **commits automatically** after each change it applies — and this course
counts commits as evidence of who did the work.

::: {.where}
VS Codium terminal
:::

```bash
git log --oneline
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b --no-auto-commits
```

::: {.warn}
Commits made by the agent are attributed to **you**. That is correct — you
directed it. But read the diff before accepting: you are answerable for every
line in your repository.
:::

## Rotate the roles

Your group logs a Driver, an Analyst and a Reporter each session.

::: {.tight}
- **Driver** writes the code
- **Analyst** decides the specification and owns the interpretation
- **Reporter** writes the three sentences and presents *if drawn*
:::

::: {.check}
Over ten sessions each of you should hold each role three or four times. Logged
in `assessment/role-logs/gNN.md` — again, your own number — checked with
`python scripts/assess.py roles`.
:::

## Why "if drawn" matters

The presenter is **drawn at random** at the start of the slot.

::: {.muted}
A group where one person understands the model has not learned the material.
The draw makes shared understanding the only viable strategy — and it is
announced now, in week two, so nobody is surprised in week twelve.
:::

# Finishing {background-color="#16181A" style="color:#F7F6F3"}

## If it breaks

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `git: command not found` | Reopen the terminal; on Windows restart VS Codium |
| Password rejected on push | Use a personal access token, not the password |
| `rejected — non-fast-forward` | `git pull` first, resolve, then push |
| Committed under the wrong email | Fix `git config`, tell me; past commits stay wrong |
| Conflict markers in a file | Delete them, keep the agreed version, add and commit |

::: {.muted}
Still stuck? Ask Qwen — it is good at git, and it runs on your laptop.
:::

- ✅ GitHub account with two-factor authentication
- ✅ **GitHub username sent to me** — you cannot push until I add you
- ✅ Course repository cloned; the Session 01 ZIP folder deleted
- ✅ Your group branch checked out — your own number, not `XX`
- ✅ One commit pushed **by you personally** to your group branch
- ✅ Your `user.name` and `user.email` written down to report
:::

"One commit pushed by you personally" means each of the three of you. Not one
